rationale:
ROUND 2 on dc62975f. Every objection was answered at the code or the live rows before being written up, and the GATING one changed the design rather than the prose.

(1) guardian HIGH — blast radius asserted, not enumerated. THE SEAT WAS RIGHT AND THE CODE HAS CHANGED. I claimed a store refusal failing the step was 'bugs_open/260's ruling applied consistently'. That was an analogy, not a measurement. Enumerated 2026-09-02: SEVEN live workflows dispatch render_site_components — nav-updater, nav-link-fixer, rerender-chrome, rerender-site, rerender-pages, pageflow-builder, site-work-orchestrator — and EVERY ONE declares no error_step, no on_error and no continue_on_error, so a hard step failure has no handler anywhere and takes the whole orchestration with it. That is new authority over seven pipelines acquired inside a bug fix, which is exactly the 2026-07-28 shape. So ESCALATION is now opt-in behind escalate_chrome_store_failure with the unsafe default OFF (the 2026-08-02 §2 remedy, and the shape of the three sibling keys in mistyped_llm_fields_gate.go). REPORTING stays unconditional, deliberately: the reporting silence IS the bug, and gating a fix for silence behind a flag nobody sets reproduces the silence. Crucially this costs nothing today — neither casualty needs the escalation, because both footers are repaired at source by UpperFirst — so the gate buys safety for free. Distinguished by a chromeStoreRefusedError sentinel so bugs_open/260's EXECUTION-failure escalation is untouched; three tests pin all three properties and two named mutations kill them.

(2) guardian MEDIUM — old call sites / summary-text consumers. VERIFIED, both halves. The emitter has exactly one pre-existing call site and it was updated in the same edit; `go build ./...` is green and committed HEAD was independently verified with scripts/verify-head-builds.sh. Consumer census for the summary text: NOTHING parses a site_work_items summary anywhere in Go, SQL or scripts — the only two matches in the estate are a commented-out note in sql_for_agents/237 about a '[stale: ...]' PREFIX on a different item type, and cmd/reasoningset/extract.sql reading da.metadata->>'summary' from a different table. Routing is by item_type and spec keys, never by summary text.

(3) bug_historian MEDIUM — was a census run for OTHER nil-swallow sites? IT HAS BEEN NOW, and it is the objection I am most glad of. Five `degraded, nil` returns in the file: :1446 is the SUCCESS return; :1407 is a lock refusal (correct — a lock is not a failure and it files its own item); :1222 is bugs_open/342's documented refusal, which reports through required_fields_missing; :1241 is 'template rendered to empty string', a Warn with its own lineage. That leaves EXACTLY ONE genuine remaining swallow: :1411, 'no row matched'. I am still not fixing it, and now I can say why with a number instead of a hunch — which is the whole point of the objection. MEASURED 2026-09-02: 57 sites exist, only 34 have any site_components rows, and 23 sites are missing at least one of the three slots. Routing :1411 into the reporting surface would therefore file up to ~69 needs_human_review items about sites that have simply never been built. The honest fix there is to distinguish 'never built' from 'the row vanished', which is a different bug with a different diagnosis; widening this one into it would trade a silent branch for a queue full of false findings. Recorded in the bug file as measured-and-deferred, not missed.

(4) bug_historian LOW — other callers relying on the old nil-swallow. renderAndStoreSiteComponent has EXACTLY ONE production caller (render_site_components_action.go:313) plus three call sites in site_component_lock_guard_test.go. There is no second consumer of the old semantics.

(5) prior_art MEDIUM — 'no gate downstream' is a load-bearing absence claim with no citation of its own. Fair. It is STY-057's stated guarantee for this exact path, quoted in grounded_in below: render_site_components 'does not store (the existing row keeps serving)' and the register entry's own landmine records that the chrome store's bytes go to the site with no validate_content between. I would add that the REFUSE choice does not actually depend on the absence being total: sanitising would leave the upstream cutter in place and silently alter bytes the site serves, which is objectionable whether or not something downstream would also have caught it.

(6) prior_art LOW — is InvalidUTF8At rebuilding dormant machinery? CENSUSED, and no. Every UTF-8 utility in the estate: platform/messaging/processor.go:638 (ToValidUTF8 — SANITISES an inbound raw body, the opposite disposition), json_envelope.go:401 (a RuneError arm inside a scanner), datahelpers/claims.go:683 and :1217 (DecodeRuneInString for windowing), namecheck.go:307 (first-rune decode). NONE reports a byte offset, and none returns a storable window. SafeCut is the sibling this is modelled on and is reused rather than duplicated.

(7) editquality MEDIUM — harvest.go asserted converted with no diff. Correct, and it is now edit 3 with its diff. It IS converted; the round-1 writeup hid a real edit behind 'outside council scope', which is the failure the seat names. The class claim can now be checked directly: `grep -rn "ToUpper(\\w*\\[:1\\])"` over non-test Go returns 1 hit and that hit is UpperFirst's OWN DOC COMMENT naming the idiom it replaces — a self-matching census I have filed as a landmine, with the positive control (9 UpperFirst references: 8 call sites + the definition) that a comment cannot satisfy.

(8) architecture LOW — sweep for other chrome slots silently degraded the same way. DONE, fleet-wide: header 34/34 rendered, head 34/34 rendered, footer 32/34 rendered. The two footers are the known casualties and there is no wider silent degradation.

NOT DONE, and I want to be explicit rather than let it read as addressed: guardian MEDIUM asked that the store-failure disposition be isolated from the byte-safety fix so a revert of one need not revert the other. This tree is forward-only (no amends, no resets) and the code was already committed as 3edb30476 when the verdict landed. The config key is the isolation I can actually deliver, and I would argue it is the better one: it isolates the risky half at RUNTIME, per step, with no revert and no roll required, which a commit boundary does not.

plan.summary: ROUND 2. The class fix and the observability fix are unchanged; the ESCALATION half is now opt-in behind escalate_chrome_store_failure (unsafe default OFF) after enumerating that all 7 workflows dispatching this action declare no error_step. Reporting stays unconditional because the silence is the bug. harvest.go is now shown rather than asserted. Eight tests total, every one mutation-proven red.

edits.symbol: UpperFirst + InvalidUTF8At (and this file's own converted call site)
edits.rationale:
The primitive. Upper-cases the FIRST RUNE, leaves the rest byte-identical, and returns already-invalid input untouched rather than substituting U+FFFD — this helper's job is not to CREATE the defect, and silently rewriting a caller's bad bytes would hide one a validator upstream should be naming. Placed beside SafeCut/TruncateString because they are the same class and a reader looking for one should find the other.

SAME FILE, also: InvalidUTF8At — The diagnostic Postgres does not give. Returns the byte offset of the first invalid sequence and a QuoteToASCII'd window (±48 bytes) around it. ASCII-only is deliberate and load-bearing: the report is logged, persisted and put in a work item summary, so a window carrying the raw bad bytes would reproduce the very defect it describes — which is precisely what the third edit below is about.

And this file's own instance of the idiom (:1980, in the display-name splitter) converted to UpperFirst, like the other seven.

edits.symbol: the live defect (:1622), half 1, the pre-store gate, the 3 truncations, the emitter phase, and NEW: the opt-in escalation gate
edits.rationale:
Unchanged from round 1 except the last item, which is the answer to the gating objection.

THE LIVE DEFECT: buildServicesHTML's word loop -> datahelpers.UpperFirst(w). Then four changes that belong in this one file and this one pass.

HALF 1 — bugs_open/423 half 1. A store that fails has exactly the disposition of a template that will not execute — previous bytes keep serving, and a site with nothing stored must not go live — so it takes the SAME surface built for bugs_open/260 rather than a second chrome-failure channel. The nil return was the enabling defect for the whole incident. NOTE THE BEHAVIOUR CHANGE: via the existing caller, a slot with nothing stored now fails the step.

THE THREE TRUNCATIONS (:1439, :1689, :1779) — The latent sibling, and it MUST land with the edit above rather than after it. emitChromeRenderFailedItem's summary interpolates an ARBITRARY error string; once the store-failure branch uses that emitter, a long error whose 248th byte falls inside a multi-byte character mints invalid UTF-8 and fails its own INSERT — the surface that REPORTS a chrome failure dying of the disease it reports, and silently, because every failure in that emitter is logged rather than returned. Uses datahelpers.SafeCut, the estate's existing truncation primitive (bugs_open/027 §4b); the 250-byte threshold is preserved exactly so no other behaviour moves.

THE GATE — The door-closer: fixing 8 call sites does not stop the 9th. REFUSE, not sanitise — argued in the rationale. Placed before the UPDATE so the report can carry an offset into the exact bytes that would have been stored, after every transform (RenderTemplate, DropDeadURLControls, injectBrandHeadTags) has run.

THE EMITTER'S PHASE — Reusing a surface means fixing its prose. Its operator-facing `fix` text said "this chrome component's template could not be executed" — false for two of its three callers now, and a queue entry that sends the next reader to the wrong half of the pipeline is the same class of defect as this bug. The phase reaches the summary and the spec; the item_key deliberately does NOT carry it, because a slot that is broken is one problem however far down the path it broke and a phase in the key would mint a second open item when the same slot failed differently on the next run.

NEW IN ROUND 2 — THE ESCALATION IS NOW OPT-IN. A chromeStoreRefusedError sentinel marks a failure that happened AFTER the template executed, and escalateUnservedChromeSlot is the deciding arm the caller consults: an EXECUTION failure escalates unconditionally (bugs_open/260's existing, reviewed authority, untouched), a STORE refusal escalates only when escalate_chrome_store_failure is set on the step. Unset means today's behaviour byte for byte across all seven workflows. Fail-OPEN on a mistyped value, like its three siblings. The arm is factored out rather than inlined so a test drives exactly what the action runs — the refusePersistForAbsentRequired precedent in this same package.

edits.symbol: the 8th call site (:411) — shown, not asserted
edits.rationale: Round 1 named this file in prose and gave no diff, and editquality was right to refuse that: either it is a real edit and belongs in the submission, or the class-fix claim is false. It is a real edit. It is the only one of the eight needing an added import, which is itself worth a reviewer seeing. Its risk is the lowest of the eight — a one-shot harvesting CLI, not a live path — but 'low risk' was never the reason to omit it; the 8-edit budget was, and that is a bookkeeping excuse for an unverifiable claim.

Two of the eight call sites, both deriving a site's LOGO TEXT from a name. Same byte slice, same failure: a company name beginning with a non-ASCII letter (an accented capital, a curly quote) is corrupted, and logo text is written to config and rendered into chrome — i.e. straight back at Postgres. Converted, not merely noted: leaving a known member of the class unfixed because it has not bitten yet is how the 2026-07-20 truncation fix missed the casing shape for six weeks.
The third logo-text derivation, in the render path itself. Same conversion, same reason as multipage_actions.go.
Call site 5 of 8. Converted in the same pass so the census can be re-run and come back clean.

Call site 6 of 8. HumaniseKey turns snake_case into a label; keys are ASCII today, so this one is a latent member rather than a live one — converted anyway, because the value of a class fix is that the next reader does not have to re-derive which members were safe. The eighth site, cmd/webdesignport/harvest.go:411, is converted identically and needed only an added datahelpers import; it is outside council scope so it has no edit of its own here.

Drives escalateUnservedChromeSlot — the arm the action calls — rather than restating its logic. (1) A store refusal does NOT escalate for nil config, empty config, explicit false, or either mistyped value; MUTATION KILLED: the gate deleted, i.e. round 1's behaviour. (2) An armed step DOES escalate; MUTATION KILLED: an arm that ignores its key, which would make the capability dead machinery — the other half of the same trap. (3) An EXECUTION failure still escalates unconditionally with nil and empty config, and a store refusal stays recognisable after being wrapped again by fmt.Errorf; MUTATION KILLED: gating the wrong half, i.e. silently withdrawing bugs_open/260's reviewed authority, and an errors.As chain that a future wrapping would defeat. Both mutations were RUN 2026-09-02 and both went red.

plan.risks:
THE ROUND-1 BEHAVIOUR CHANGE IS NOW GATED AND THE RISK IS LARGELY WITHDRAWN. With escalate_chrome_store_failure unset — which is every step today — a store refusal reports and does not fail anybody's build, so none of the seven workflows changes behaviour. garden-tools.uk's build no longer starts failing, and its footer is repaired at source regardless.

What remains: the key must not be armed by a migration until a chassis image carrying this code has rolled, or it is a no-op that LOOKS applied (the 502 ordering rule this estate has been bitten by). Nothing arms it in this change, deliberately.

The gate REFUSES invalid UTF-8 rather than sanitising. If a future producer legitimately needs lossy repair, this is the wrong place for it — the repair belongs at the producer, and this gate is what will name the producer.

The 8-site conversion is behaviour-preserving only on ASCII, pinned by test. On non-ASCII the output changes from corrupt to correct; any consumer depending on the corrupted form would break, and none can exist, because such a string could not have round-tripped through Postgres.

:1411 stays a silent swallow by a measured decision (23 of 57 sites would generate false findings). It is named in the bug file so the next reader inherits the measurement rather than the omission.

Go, so inert until the next chassis roll.
